blocks.content: Quiz: Why are LandingNavbar and the AppLayout navigation built as completely separate components in SpeedBlip?
Tap an option below to answer:
React does not support conditional rendering of navigation components inside a shared layout
React fully supports conditional rendering. The separation is an intentional architectural decision, not a React limitation.
React fully supports conditional rendering. The separation is an intentional architectural decision, not a React limitation.
The LandingNavbar needs different CSS that conflicts with the AppLayout sidebar styles
CSS conflicts can be scoped at the component level. The separation exists because the two navigations serve completely different purposes and should never render simultaneously.
CSS conflicts can be scoped at the component level. The separation exists because the two navigations serve completely different purposes and should never render simultaneously.
They serve different purposes and React Router's layout nesting ensures they never render on the wrong route

Correct. LandingNavbar is a marketing navigation with CTAs. AppLayout navigation is a route-aware app shell. Mixing them in one component would require complex conditional logic - separation is cleaner and more maintainable.

Correct. LandingNavbar is a marketing navigation with CTAs. AppLayout navigation is a route-aware app shell. Mixing them in one component would require complex conditional logic - separation is cleaner and more maintainable.
Netlify requires separate components for marketing and app pages to enable split routing
Netlify's routing has no influence on how React components are structured. This is a front-end architecture decision, not a hosting requirement.
Netlify's routing has no influence on how React components are structured. This is a front-end architecture decision, not a hosting requirement.
